findings.reason: the section must first state why the existing `_reuse_covered` path does not already skip the warm walk for the roadmap reader the profile measured (a bug in it, or a reader that never sets `revalidate=True`), or the section is building a second walk-skip beside a working one.
findings.text: §3's premise, that the warm covered-tree walk runs `_walk_covered` on every call with nothing to skip it, misses the walk-avoidance already in the file: `_reuse_covered` (metadata_index.py:215-240) compares each recorded directory identity (`_dir_identity`, metadata_index.py:490) against the persisted `dir_stamps` and, when the tree shape is unchanged, hands `build_index` the file set (`covered=`/`dirs=`, metadata_index.py:306-325) so `_walk_covered` (metadata_index.py:423) is never called — reached on the MCP path at `mcp_views.py:1180` (`index_rows(..., revalidate=True)`).

findings.reason: the section must reconcile with the existing in-process cache (the measured 6.4 s may be `_git_head`'s uncached `git rev-parse HEAD` at serve.py:1244, not the date maps), or it adds a third layer over the same answers.
findings.text: §4 proposes "an in-process memo keyed on the repository's `HEAD` and the path" for git dates and does not cite the in-process HEAD-gated map already present: `_GIT_CREATION_CACHE` (serve.py:1279-1288, populated at serve.py:1311) returns `dict(cached.times)` with no git call when `cached.head == head`, and `_GIT_LAST_MODIFIED_CACHE` (serve.py:1316) mirrors it; both sit in front of the persistent caches at serve.py:1121 and serve.py:1324, exactly the two-level shape §4 describes.

findings.reason: the deliverable and its negative control are unsound as written — routing both through `read_state_and_text_file` is one way to unify the kind, but "restore `read_authored` to its own read" cannot make the parse count rise because it is already memoised, so the stated negative control would not fire.
findings.text: §5's premise is false for both sites it names: `read_authored` already reads through the path-keyed memo (`memoized("section_authored", path, read_authored)`, roadmap.py:184) and `_read_readiness_uncached` is already wrapped by `memoized("readiness_state", path, ...)` (serve.py:2067); neither "reads and parses itself" outside `file_memo`. The real cost is that the same file is parsed once per distinct `kind` (`section_authored`, `readiness_state`, `read_state_and_text`) instead of once.

findings.reason: the honest change extends `_reuse_covered` in `metadata_index.py` (or fixes the reader that bypasses it), not a parallel identity map in `file_memo`.
findings.text: §3 places the walk memo in `reckon/file_memo.py` keyed on directory stat identity, duplicating the owner of that mechanism: `_dir_identity` (metadata_index.py:490) + `_reuse_covered` (metadata_index.py:215) + the persisted `dir_stamps` (metadata_index.py:748, 783) already key the file set on exactly those mtimes/inodes; a second copy in `file_memo` means two directory-identity implementations that can drift.

findings.reason: the section should extend `_GIT_CREATION_CACHE`/`_GIT_LAST_MODIFIED_CACHE` (or memoise `_git_head`) rather than fork a second cache answering the same question.
findings.text: §4 places the in-process git-date memo in `reckon/serve.py` beside the existing owner of that responsibility — `_GIT_CREATION_CACHE` / `_GIT_LAST_MODIFIED_CACHE` (serve.py:1279, 1316) — which already hold the HEAD-keyed answers the plan wants to add, so the plan would leave two in-process caches of the same git dates in one module.

findings.reason: the plan must justify the wrapper over extending the mechanism that already skips the walk, or delete it.
findings.text: §3 adds a thin memo layer over `_walk_covered` without saying why `_walk_covered`'s existing caller-side skip (`_reuse_covered`) cannot be extended; the wrapper forwards the walk's result to a new store and adds surface without adding depth.

findings.reason: the plan should extend the existing cache or memoise the uncached `_git_head` call, and say which, rather than add a parallel front layer.
findings.text: §4 adds a thin memo layer in front of the git-date caches without saying why the existing in-process caches cannot be extended to cover the measured cost; the layer forwards to the same machinery.

rubric_items.deep_module: pass — no new module is proposed; §2–§5 are point changes inside existing modules, so there is no new shallow-wrapper spread to weigh.
rubric_items.duplicate_owner: a finding — §3 re-owns directory-identity walk-avoidance already owned by `reckon/metadata_index.py`, and §4 re-owns the HEAD-keyed git-date in-process cache already owned by `reckon/serve.py`.
rubric_items.interface_budget: pass — public_definitions 1626, cli_options 351, mcp_views 33, refusal_families 23; no section adds a CLI option, MCP view, refusal family or public definition (each reuses the existing `file_memo.memoized`, `index_rows` and serve helpers), so no section owes a retirement or merge to account for.
rubric_items.reuse_search: a finding — §3, §4 and §5 each add a mechanism (walk memo, in-process git-date memo, per-file parse memo) whose equivalent already exists in the codebase they extend, and none cites it.
rubric_items.thin_wrapper: a finding — §3 and §4 add thin memo layers in front of existing machinery (`_walk_covered`, the git-date caches) without saying why that machinery cannot simply be extended.
